intro: This unit follows one secret criminal society, the Sicilian Mafia, from the lemon groves around Palermo in the 1860s to courtrooms in Palermo and Chicago. The story reaches into our own time. You will meet the people who studied it, the people who feared it and the people who stood up to it. You will also meet Chinese American tongs and the triads, and see how their story differs.

The Mafia's strongest shield was omertà, a rule of silence. For more than a century it kept witnesses quiet and crimes unpunished. This unit is about how that silence was broken: by police reports, Senate hearings, new laws, brave insiders, judges who paid with their lives and ordinary neighbors acting together. Remember too that almost all Italian Americans and Chinese Americans had nothing to do with these groups, and many were their victims.

By the end, you will be able to explain where the Mafia came from and how it spread. You will be able to describe how the RICO Act and the Maxi Trial worked. You will also be able to weigh an insider's testimony, and to explain the real cost of organized crime to ordinary people.
bigQuestion: How did people break the Mafia's rule of silence, and what did it cost them?

timeline.t: Leopoldo Franchetti and Sidney Sonnino travel Sicily; their study is published in 1877
Palermo police chief Ermanno Sangiorgi maps eight Mafia groups and 218 men
The Kefauver Committee holds hearings in about 14 cities, including Chicago
A state police roadblock at Apalachin, New York, exposes a meeting of crime leaders
Joseph Valachi testifies on television and names Cosa Nostra
The RICO Act becomes law as part of the Organized Crime Control Act
The Maxi Trial opens in Palermo's bunker courtroom, with 475 people charged
The Maxi Trial court convicts more than 330 people; 19 get life sentences
Italy's Court of Cassation upholds the Maxi Trial verdict
Judges Giovanni Falcone and Paolo Borsellino are murdered with members of their escorts
Young people in Palermo post Addiopizzo stickers against protection money
Chicago's Operation Family Secrets jury convicts leaders of the Outfit

words.d: the Mafia's rule of silence: never help the police or the courts
a deal where people pay a group so the group will not harm them
Mafia groups or clans in Sicily, each with its own territory; one group is a cosca
Italian for 'our thing'; the name members use for the Mafia
a group of people working together; here, criminals working together
a person who gives inside information about a group to the authorities
a Chinese American association or hall; most began to help members, and some ran illegal businesses
members of a group helping each other with needs such as jobs, money, housing and burial
the 1970 U.S. law that makes it a crime to run or take part in a criminal enterprise
Italian for a Mafia member who turns and cooperates with the authorities
evidence from another source that supports what a witness says
protection money that the Mafia demands from shops and businesses

test.q: In which decades did the Sicilian Mafia first grow in western Sicily?
test.why: Records place the Mafia's start in the decades after Italian unification in 1860.

test.q: What did Franchetti and Sangiorgi each provide?
choices: Early written evidence of how the Mafia worked in Sicily
test.why: Franchetti's 1877 study and Sangiorgi's 1898 to 1900 reports are early written records of the Mafia.

choices: A rank in a crime family
The rule of silence toward police and courts
test.why: Omertà is the Mafia's rule never to help the police or courts.

test.q: Which event exposed a meeting of crime leaders from many states?
test.why: Sergeant Croswell's roadblock at Apalachin identified 58 men from many states.

test.q: Which statement about the Kefauver Committee is true?
choices: It held hearings in about 14 cities, including Chicago
It was a criminal trial with a jury
test.why: The committee held hearings in about 14 cities from 1950 to 1951, Chicago among them.

test.q: Who gave the American public the name Cosa Nostra in 1963?
test.why: Valachi told the McClellan subcommittee that members called the organization Cosa Nostra.

test.q: How did most Chinese American tongs begin?
choices: As branches of the Sicilian Mafia
As mutual-aid associations for immigrants shut out by exclusion laws
test.why: Tongs began mostly as mutual-aid groups when exclusion laws and prejudice shut Chinese immigrants out.

test.q: What does RICO let prosecutors do?
choices: Charge people for running or taking part in an enterprise through a pattern of crimes
test.why: RICO targets running or taking part in an enterprise through a pattern of racketeering activity.

test.q: Why did the Palermo magistrates work as a pool?
choices: So that killing one of them could not stop the investigation
So they could work in Rome instead
test.why: Chinnici's idea was that shared files meant no single death could stop the work.

test.q: What did Tommaso Buscetta explain to Falcone?
choices: How to build a bunker courtroom
How Cosa Nostra was organized into families, districts and a Commission
How to write the RICO Act
test.why: Buscetta described families, districts and a ruling Commission.

choices: Italy's highest court upheld the Maxi Trial verdict
test.why: The Court of Cassation upheld the verdict on 30 January 1992.

test.q: What did the Addiopizzo stickers say, in English?
choices: Pay the pizzo and stay safe
A whole people who pays the pizzo is a people without dignity
test.why: That is the English meaning of the Italian sentence on the 2004 stickers.

test.q: In Operation Family Secrets, what did Frank Calabrese Jr. do?
choices: Wore a wire and testified against his father
test.why: Calabrese Jr. recorded conversations with his father and later testified in court.

test.q: Which is the best example of corroboration?
choices: A witness repeats his own story twice
A bank record confirms a payment a witness described
test.why: Corroboration is evidence from another source, such as a bank record, that supports a witness.

test.q: Which statement best fits the evidence in this unit about Italian Americans?
choices: Most were part of crime families
The Kefauver report proved all were connected
Most had nothing to do with crime, and many were its victims or fought it
None were ever victims of the Black Hand
test.why: The unit shows most Italian Americans were not involved, and many were victims or fought back.

write.prompt: Which did more to weaken the Mafia: new laws and trials, or ordinary people breaking silence? Take a side. Use at least three facts or sources from the unit, such as RICO, the Maxi Trial, Buscetta, Addiopizzo or Family Secrets, and answer the strongest point on the other side.
tips: Name your sources, such as the Sangiorgi report, the Kefauver report or the Maxi Trial verdict.
Give the other side fairly before you answer it.
Use the unit's terms, such as omertà, RICO, pentito and corroboration.
Keep the focus on the people who resisted, not on the bosses.
When numbers differ between sources, say so.
